claims.text: A homogeneous dispersion of nano-Y2O3 particles preferentially located at grain boundaries stabilizes grain boundaries in ODS tungsten at high temperature.
Grain-boundary-localized nano-Y2O3 particles impede void nucleation.
A homogeneous Y2O3 dispersion promotes grain-boundary sliding in ODS tungsten at high temperature.
A homogeneous Y2O3 dispersion facilitates dislocation climb in ODS tungsten at high temperature.
The promoted grain-boundary sliding and dislocation climb constitute a dynamic-recovery process.
This dynamic-recovery process prevents premature grain-boundary failure.
Preventing premature grain-boundary failure produces more uniform plastic flow.
A homogeneous grain-boundary Y2O3 dispersion increases plastic strain-to-failure relative to minimal or inhomogeneous oxide dispersion.
A homogeneous grain-boundary Y2O3 dispersion improves toughness relative to minimal or inhomogeneous oxide dispersion.
The engineered alloy will exhibit delayed cavitation onset relative to the baseline.
The engineered alloy will exhibit a more homogeneous grain-boundary strain distribution than the baseline.
Premature grain-boundary cavitation is the typical high-temperature failure mechanism in the baseline tungsten alloy with minimal or inhomogeneous Y2O3 dispersion.
The proposed mechanism governs behavior over the 900–1300°C temperature range.
Oxide-dispersion strengthening is influential in tungsten-based systems within the stated high-temperature domain.
The controlled comparison is intended to hold grain size and tungsten-matrix composition similar while varying Y2O3 dispersion.
Failure to obtain statistically significant improvements in strain-to-failure or toughness, or failure to observe delayed cavitation, is defined as falsifying the proposed mechanism.
